content.comment_body: When configuring [product_name] in ETS to send a value from KNX to [product_name], and it's a 2-byte float (to variable memory), I notice the value is automatically rounded by [product_name]. For example, a temperature of 13.4°C in KNX is shown as 13°C in [product_name]. Is there a way to preserve fractional digits in the float value? The [product_name] manual mentions: When handling floating-point values, the interpolation points on the KNX side can have decimal places, but values sent to [product_name] are rounded off by [product_name] if needed.

[product_name] can only process integer values (whole numbers), and does not support real numbers (floating point). I do not have experience with KNX or ETS software. Are you able to multiply the value on the KNX side by 10? If so, you could represent a decimal place within [product_name]—at least for display purposes.
Good point. I configured [product_name] in ETS to multiply the number by 10, so for example, 12.5°C gets represented as 125 in [product_name]. This solution works as intended now.

analysis.insight_summary: Users face a limitation when integrating KNX with [company_name] products: these devices only process integer values, so floating-point numbers received from KNX are automatically rounded. This restricts precise measurement needs and leads users to seek alternative ways to retain the decimal information.
analysis.user_expectations: Users prefer these devices to accept and process floating-point values with their fractional digits preserved, ensuring accurate data transfer from KNX without losing precision.
